title: A ration card and the Right to Information
body: Nannu, a daily wage earner living in a slum colony in East Delhi, lost his ration card and applied for a duplicate one. For three months he kept visiting the local Food and Civil Supplies office, but the clerks and officials neither did his work nor told him the status of his application. He then filed an application under the Right to Information Act, asking for the daily progress on his application, the names of the officials responsible for it and the action that would be taken against them for their inaction. Within a week, an inspector visited him to say that his card was ready. When he went to collect it, the senior officer received him warmly, offered him tea and requested him to withdraw his application under the Right to Information, since his work had now been done.
